claims.claim: The CLI binary is named `promptarena`
PromptArena runs multi-turn conversation simulations across multiple LLM providers, validates conversation flows, and generates test reports
Usage pattern is `promptarena [command] [flags]`
Command `init` initializes a new Arena test project from a template (built-in or remote)
Command `agent-brief` writes the AI coding-agent brief (AGENTS.md + .claude/skills/) into a project
Command `templates` manages templates with subcommands list, fetch, update, render, repo
Command `run` runs conversation simulations (main command)
Command `generate` generates scenario files from session data or external sources
Command `mocks` generates mock provider responses from Arena JSON results
Command `config-inspect` inspects and validates configuration
Command `debug` debugs configuration and prompt loading
Command `prompt-debug` debugs and tests prompt generation
Command `chat` talks live to an agent defined in the Arena config through an interactive TUI
Command `serve` starts the live web UI with SSE streaming and a REST API
Command `validate` validates configuration files
Command `calibrate` scores a check, such as an LLM judge, against examples a person has labeled
Command `view` browses and views past test results in the TUI
Command `export` exports an arena config as a PromptPack JSON file
Command `deploy` deploys prompt packs to cloud providers via adapter plugins
Command `mcp` runs an MCP server exposing PromptArena authoring knowledge over stdio
Command `explain` explains a PromptArena authoring concept
Command `schema` prints the embedded JSON schema for a config type
Command `examples` lists and prints the example kits embedded in the binary
Command `personas` copies built-in self-play personas, such as red-team attackers, into a project
Command `skill` manages shared AgentSkills.io skills with install, list and remove
Command `completion` generates a shell autocompletion script
Command `help` shows help about any command
Global flag `-h, --help` shows help for promptarena
Command form `promptarena init [directory] [flags]`
Flag `--quick` (bool) skips interactive prompts and uses defaults
Flag `--quick` defaults to false
Flag `--provider` (string) selects the provider to configure
Flag `--provider` accepts the values mock, openai, claude, gemini
Flag `--provider` has no default value
Flag `--template` (string) selects the template to use for initialization
Flag `--template` defaults to quick-start
Flag `--template-index` (string) takes a template repo name or index URL/path for remote templates
Flag `--template-index` defaults to community
Flag `--repo-config` (string) sets the template repo config file
Flag `--repo-config` defaults to the user config file
Flag `--template-cache` (string) sets the cache directory for remote templates
Flag `--template-cache` defaults to a temp directory
Flag `--output` (string) sets the output directory
Flag `--output` defaults to the current directory `.`
Flag `--no-agent` (bool) skips writing the AI-agent brief (AGENTS.md + .claude/skills/)
Flag `--no-agent` defaults to false
Flag `--no-env` (bool) skips .env file creation
Flag `--no-env` defaults to false
Flag `--no-git` (bool) skips git initialization
Flag `--no-git` defaults to false
Flag `--verbose` (bool) shows detailed generation progress for init
Flag `--verbose` on init defaults to false
PromptArena includes 6 built-in templates
Built-in template `quick-start` generates 6 files

Built-in template `code-assistant` generates 9 files
Built-in template `content-generation` generates 9 files
Built-in template `multimodal` generates 7 files
Built-in template `mcp-integration` generates 7 files

`promptarena templates list --index internal` lists templates from the named repo internal
`promptarena templates list --index community` lists templates using the community shorthand
`promptarena init my-test --quick` creates a project with the quick-start template and defaults
`promptarena init my-test --quick --provider openai` creates a project configured for the openai provider
`promptarena init my-test --quick --template customer-support --provider openai` uses the customer-support template

init creates `config.arena.yaml` as the main Arena configuration
init creates a `prompts/` directory
init creates a `providers/` directory
init creates a `scenarios/` directory
init creates a `tools/` directory for tool definitions (customer-support template)
init creates a `.env` file with API key placeholders

serve has a flag `--open`

Flag `--input, -i` (string) takes an Arena JSON result file or a directory containing *.json runs

Flag `--output, -o` (string) takes an output file path, or a directory when --per-scenario is set
Flag `--output` defaults to `providers/mock-generated.yaml`
Flag `--per-scenario` (bool) writes one YAML file per scenario into the --output directory
Flag `--per-scenario` defaults to false
Flag `--merge` (bool) merges with existing mock files instead of overwriting
Flag `--merge` defaults to false
Flag `--scenario` (string list) includes only the specified scenario IDs
Flag `--scenario` has no default (all scenarios)
Flag `--provider` (string list) includes only the specified provider IDs in mocks generate

Flag `--dry-run` (bool) prints the generated YAML instead of writing files

generate creates Arena scenario YAML from recorded sessions or external session sources using pluggable SessionSourceAdapter implementations
generate is useful for turning production conversations with failing assertions into reproducible test scenarios
Command form `promptarena generate [flags]`
Flag `--from-recordings` (string) takes a glob of local recordings
Flag `--from-recordings` has no default
Flag `--source` (string) selects an installed deploy adapter to pull sessions from (example: omnia)
Flag `--source` has no default
--source needs the adapter's `sessions` capability and a `deploy:` section in --config for endpoint, workspace and token
Flag `--workspace` (string) overrides the deploy profile's workspace when using --source
Flag `--workspace` has no default
Flag `--filter-passed` (bool) filters by pass/fail status and is tri-state: omitted for all, true for passed, false for failed
Flag `--filter-passed` has no default (tri-state, omitted means all sessions)
Flag `--filter-eval-type` (string) filters sessions by assertion failure type, e.g. content_matches
Flag `--filter-eval-type` has no default
Flag `--expect` (repeatable string) sets an expected range for a measured eval, e.g. faithfulness>=0.8
--expect selects sessions whose score fell outside the range and becomes the generated assertion's min_score/max_score
Flag `--expect` has no default
Flag `--config` (string) names an arena config whose pack supplies eval params and declared thresholds for recorded measurements
Flag `--config` has no default for generate
Flag `--task-type` (string) sets task_type on generated scenarios
Flag `--task-type` defaults to conversation
A recorded workflow entry state's prompt_task takes precedence over --task-type
Flag `--output` (string) sets the output directory for generated scenario files in generate
generate --output defaults to `.`
Flag `--dedup` (bool) deduplicates sessions by failure pattern fingerprint
Flag `--dedup` defaults to true
`--pack` is a deprecated alias for `--task-type` and only ever set the task type
generate requires either --from-recordings or --source
--from-recordings reads local files, while --source <name> resolves an installed deploy adapter
The --source adapter is resolved from ~/.promptarena/adapters/promptarena-deploy-<name> or a project-local adapters folder
--source hands the adapter the merged deploy config from --config, including the token stored by `promptarena deploy login`
An adapter without the sessions capability is reported along with the upgrade command
--from-recordings accepts a glob and picks a reader per file
Arena run output input is `out/*.json`, one file per run as written by `promptarena run`
Arena run output carries messages with tool calls and results, scenario and provider, and conversation-level and per-turn assertion results
Failed assertions in Arena run output become the generated scenario's assertions with their original parameters
PromptKit session recording input is `*.recording.json` or the event store `*.jsonl`
PromptKit session recordings carry no assertion results, so --filter-passed treats every session as passing
Doc link /arena/how-to/scenarios/session-recording/ points to an existing page
Transcript input is `*.transcript.yaml` and carries messages only
Pointing generate at the out/ directory of a run with failures produces one scenario per failing run
Every user turn in a session becomes a scenario turn, including attached images, documents and audio
A session with several user turns is generated in full, with a warning in the output and in the scenario description
The recorded pack identity and template variables are carried into the generated scenario
A recorded workflow entry state becomes the scenario's task_type
Recorded sessions hold measurements (scores) rather than verdicts, and a scenario assertion is the same eval type and params plus min_score/max_score
A recorded eval whose verdict (assertion or guardrail) failed is asserted with its recorded params
A recorded eval whose verdict passed is dropped
A pack threshold declared for the eval (via --config) produces an assertion with that bound
An --expect bound for the eval produces an assertion with that bound
With no verdict, threshold or --expect, the eval is reported with its score and the --expect to pass, and never asserted against an invented bound
The operators >= and > become min_score; <= and < become max_score; == sets both
Bounds are inclusive, so a strict operator is widened and the decision says so
--expect also selects sessions: only those whose measurement fell outside the range (or never produced one) are generated
Every fetched session is checked against the expectations again, even when the source filters on its side
A session inside every expected range is skipped with a warning naming the expectations
Output decision label `asserted-threshold` is printed for an eval asserted from a pack threshold
Output decision label `reported` is printed when no threshold is known, suggesting --expect or a threshold on the eval in the pack
`promptarena generate --from-recordings "out/*.json" --filter-passed=false --output scenarios/generated` turns failing runs into scenarios
`promptarena generate --from-recordings "recordings/*.recording.json" --output scenarios/generated` generates from PromptKit session recordings
`promptarena generate --from-recordings "out/*.json" --filter-eval-type content_matches --output scenarios/content-failures` filters by assertion failure type

`promptarena generate --from-recordings "out/*.json" --config config.arena.yaml --expect faithfulness>=0.8 --output scenarios/faithfulness-regressions` turns sessions where faithfulness fell below 0.8 into scenarios that assert >=0.8, using the pack's eval params
Example text: the --task-type flag sets the task type the generated scenarios run against
`promptarena generate --from-recordings "out/*.json" --task-type support --output scenarios/support` sets task_type to support

`promptarena generate --source omnia --config arena.yaml --filter-passed=false --expect faithfulness>=0.8 --output scenarios/production-failures` pulls failing sessions through the installed omnia deploy adapter
Doc link /arena/how-to/scenarios/generate-from-production-sessions/ points to an existing page

built-in persona registry name `crescendo`
crescendo uses gradual escalation in small steps, each building on the agent's last reply (arXiv 2404.01833)
built-in persona registry name `refine`
refine rewrites each turn from the last response and check results (PAIR, arXiv 2310.08419)
built-in persona registry name `multi-technique`
multi-technique reasons about the last response, then picks from an editable list of conversational techniques (GOAT, arXiv 2410.01606)
built-in persona registry name `adversarial-scaffold`
adversarial-scaffold wires every variable in and leaves the method for the user to write
built-in persona registry name `direct`
direct asks for the objective once, plainly, and is meant for objectives marked baseline: true
objective field `baseline: true` marks an objective for the direct persona

redteam writes scenarios/<name>-over-refusal.scenario.yaml holding the benign requests

redteam prints the scenarios, self_play and judges entries to add to the arena config
scripted strategy sends the row's prompt, or its objective when it has none, as a scripted user turn through the converter
scripted turn assertions are content_excludes on the success pattern, the judge scoring below 0.5, or refusal when neither is set
persona strategy puts the built-in persona on a self-play turn with an objective, expect not_achieved and a rewind on refusal of at most 3
persona strategy success checks are content_includes on the row's success_pattern and, with --judge, an llm_judge scoring 0.5 or more
a persona strategy needs at least one of success_pattern or --judge
the baseline asks the objective once with the direct persona and baseline: true, with the same checks
with no success pattern and no judge, the baseline check is refusal with max_score 0
over-refusal scenario sends each benign request with a refusal assertion at max_score 0, which passes when the agent answers

promptarena skill [subcommand] [flags] is the usage form of the skill command
promptarena skill install is a subcommand that installs a skill from a Git repository or local path
promptarena skill list is a subcommand that lists installed skills
promptarena skill remove is a subcommand that removes an installed skill
promptarena skill install <ref> [flags] is the usage form of install
The @org/name reference installs the latest version from https://github.com/org/name
The @org/name@version reference installs a specific Git tag or ref
The ./path/to/skill reference installs from a local directory
Flag --project (type bool) installs to project-level .promptkit/skills/ instead of user-level
--project defaults to false
Flag --into (type string) installs directly into a specified directory
--into has no default value
--into and --project are mutually exclusive
User-level (default) skills install to ~/.config/promptkit/skills/org/name/
Project-level (--project) skills install to .promptkit/skills/org/name/
Custom (--into dir) skills install to dir/name/
The user-level skills directory respects the XDG_CONFIG_HOME environment variable
promptarena skill install @anthropic/pdf-processing is a valid command
promptarena skill install @anthropic/pdf-processing@v1.0.0 is a valid command pinning a tag
promptarena skill install ./path/to/skill is a valid command
promptarena skill install @anthropic/pdf-processing --project is a valid command
promptarena skill install @anthropic/pci-compliance --into ./skills/billing is a valid command
Example skill references @anthropic/pdf-processing and @anthropic/pci-compliance resolve to GitHub repositories
promptarena skill list is a valid command
skill list groups installed skills by location (Project and User)
Project-level skill listing shows path .promptkit/skills/anthropic/pci-compliance for @anthropic/pci-compliance
User-level skill listing shows path ~/.config/promptkit/skills/anthropic/pdf-processing for @anthropic/pdf-processing
